items.title: Chinese AI Chipmakers Poised to Gain From Beijing’s Tech Push
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s AI chip designers are expecting bumper sales this earnings season off the back of Beijing’s push to get local firms to use homegrown components and reduce their reliance on American tech.</article>

items.title: BMI's Chowdhury on Copper, Gold, Oil Markets
items.content: <article>Sabrin Chowdhury, Head of Commodities Research at BMI, discusses the outlook for precious metals and oil markets following reports that Iran attacked “hostile targets” in the Strait of Hormuz. She speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts on Bloomberg: The Asia Trade. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Jane Street Joins $2 Billion Group With Bet on Australia AI
items.author: Ambereen Choudhury and Ainslie Chandler
items.content: <article>Jane Street is among a group of investors committing $2 billion to Australian data center company Firmus Technologies Pty, marking the trading behemoth’s latest bet on the country’s fast-growing artificial intelligence sector.</article>

items.title: SK Hynix Directs Chip Windfall Into Korean Corporate Bond Market
items.author: Haram Lim and Hooyeon Kim
items.content: <article>The AI boom has prompted global tech giants to raise billions issuing bonds, but for at least one major manufacturer the involvement in credit markets doesn’t stop there.</article>

items.title: Tencent AI Spending Key After Magnificent 7 Rout
items.author: Rachel Yeo
items.content: <article>Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s spending plans will draw investor scrutiny as investors cool on lavish outlays on artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: Atlassian Shares Surge as Revenue Jump Douses AI Fears
items.author: Peter Vercoe
items.content: <article>Atlassian Corp. shares surged in after-hours trading after quarterly revenue climbed, easing concerns that the software services company would be overtaken by artificial intelligence applications.</article>

items.title: Markets Slip as Rising Yields Pressure Tech | The Close 8/6/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Kestra Investment Management CIO Kara Murphy, e.l.f. Beauty CEO Tarang Amin, Klaviyo CEO & Co-Founder Andrew Bialecki, CAIS Founder, Chairman, & CEO Matt Brown, Manulife John Hancock Investments Co-Chief Investment Strategist Emily Roland, Placer.ai Analytical Research Head R.J. Hottovy, GoodRx CEO Wendy Barnes, Elanco Animal Health President & CEO Jeff Simmons, RXO CEO Drew Wilkerson, & The Conference Board CEO Steve Odland.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Conference Board CEO on C-Suite Optimism, Hiring Plans
items.content: <article>Steve Odland, CEO of the Conference Board, discussed the latest CEO confidence survey results, which showed an increase from 47 to 52 between the second and third quarters of 2026, moving the index into positive territory. The second quarter's negative reading was largely attributed to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly the war in Iran and the resulting spike in oil prices to around $120 per barrel. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: RXO CEO on Earnings Beat, Freight Market Outlook
items.content: <article>RXO, a leading freight broker, reported second quarter results showing a 25% increase in revenue and adjusted EPS exceeding analyst estimates by 6 cents. CEO Drew Wilkerson highlighted that the company is in the early stages of a freight recovery, driven by a significant rise in spot rates that currently outperform contract rates. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: CAIS CEO Talks New Funding Round, AI’s Fintech Impact
items.content: <article>Matt Brown, Founder, Chairman, and CEO of CAIS, discussed the company's recent $170 million Series D funding round led by Vista and supported by Allianz Bernstein, Blue Owl, and Carlyle, which values the alternative asset investment platform at over $2 billion—more than double its previous valuation. Brown highlighted CAIS's 37% organic growth and explained that the new capital will be used to pursue strategic mergers and acquisitions in response to ongoing fintech industry consolidation, enhance AI capabilities to improve the platform's user experience for advisers and asset managers, and provide liquidity to long-term shareholders through an institutional tender offer facilitated by Nasdaq Private Markets. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Klaviyo CEO on Revenue Growth, E-Commerce Outlook
items.content: <article>Andrew Bialecki, CEO of Klaviyo, discussed the company's recent financial performance and growth strategy following a quarter with 26% revenue growth, reaching an almost $1.5 billion run rate. Despite a sequential slowdown from previous higher growth rates, Bialecki emphasized the company's durable growth driven by a broad customer base of over 205,000 businesses, including new large clients such as Warner Music Group and the San Francisco 49ers. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Google’s Shakeup Complicates Race With OpenAI, Anthropic
items.author: Shirin Ghaffary
items.content: <article>The tech giant is entering a new period of transition.</article>

items.title: Cloudflare Lifts Annual Profit Outlook, Beats Wall Street Target
items.author: Ignacio Gonzalez
items.content: <article>Cloudflare Inc. gave a forecast for profit this year that topped Wall Street’s estimates, suggesting that demand for networking services continued to accelerate amid rapid adoption of artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: Fed Silence & Tightening Spread Environment | Real Yield 8/6/2026
items.content: <article>"Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: JPMorgan Asset Management Head of Market Strategy, Alternative Fixed Income Oksana Aronov and BNP Paribas Global Head, Desk Analysy Viktor Hjort.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Lyft Delivers Bookings Beat With Premium Rides, Misses on Income
items.author: Natalie Lung
items.content: <article>Lyft Inc.’s second-quarter bookings beat expectations, thanks to growing demand for premium rides and strength in European markets, while net income missed estimates.</article>

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices to Buy Startup Taalas for New AI Chips
items.author: Ian King
items.content: <article>Advanced Micro Devices Inc. is buying Canadian startup Taalas, a move that will let it offer another type of artificial intelligence chip to the burgeoning data center industry.</article>

items.title: Hackers Target Wall Street in New Set of Attacks
items.content: <article>Hackers launched a wave of sophisticated attacks on Wall Street firms in recent days, according to people familiar. Hedge funds have been the main target. Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence takes a closer look at what companies are doing to try and protect themselves and how stocks could be impacted. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Stocks Extend Losses as Rate-Hike, Mideast Concerns Weigh
items.author: Joel Leon
items.content: <article>US stocks extended declines on Thursday as investors grappled with concerns over an interest-rate hike and rising geopolitical risk.</article>

items.title: China’s Unitree Seeks $904 Million in First Mainland Robotic IPO
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>China’s Yushu Technology Co., known as Unitree Robotics, is seeking to raise about 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that would make it the mainland’s first publicly traded humanoid robot maker.</article>

items.title: Peloton Gives Disappointing Outlook in Blow to Comeback Bid
items.author: Samantha Murphy Kelly
items.content: <article>Peloton Interactive Inc. gave a revenue forecast for the fiscal 2027 year that disappointed investors, marking the latest setback for the fitness technology company.</article>
